tool_args.rationale: All five paid observations are at H ≤ 0.48, while the target is H = 22.3. The pilot supports a sink-coupled response but does not establish whether slow adaptation overtakes the fast gain. The long-horizon probe directly tests that uncertainty before model confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At short horizons, the slow term depends mainly on the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. A pilot fit can therefore leave the forecast at H = 22.3 poorly constrained.
It captures a possible late reversal but omits the gradient dependence indicated by the pilot.
The pilot provides no evidence of recurring oscillation and instead points to gradient-dependent suppression.
Finer trajectory sampling is less directly informative about the slow term at the target horizon.
It does not resolve the slow-horizon ambiguity.
